note: Machine-readable copy of the site verdicts written in records/01-probe-characterization.md. The prose record is authoritative; revise both together. The probe report renders these verdicts on each probe page so that a reader sees what was concluded, by what evidence, and what would overturn it.

site.name: Site A
site.confidence: Medium for the verdict; high that this is not concealment
evidence: The answering range is exactly the eight /24s announced by AS400050, and ology.com resolves into it: a named, public, ordinary web host rather than a hidden one.
One certificate covered 237 addresses and expired in May 2025: an abandoned deployment, not an active watch post.
The whole range answers with one page and any Host header, which is configuration, not deliberation.
Group 1 is not excluded: a party watching a range would answer it exactly like this. The awareness test has not been run.
site.falsifier: Withdrawal of the announcement with the answers persisting would break the reading; evidence of the service reacting to our probes would move it to curious; a renewed certificate and a live site would make it an ordinary service with a stale record.

site.name: Site B
site.verdict: Two claims: incidental for the anomaly, nefarious for the activity
site.confidence: Medium; abuse of a reseller's host cannot be separated from a deliberate operator without the provider's records
evidence: The /24 is announced by a hosting provider while the delegation file calls the whole /22 reserved: the anomaly itself is a records artifact.

The activity is not: an automatic redirect page loading car.js, a throwaway domain farm in the certificate (baidu.sina.2022.5508085.com and two siblings), an unconfigured Apache host on the same /24, and no reverse DNS anywhere.
Nobody needs that combination to be found.
site.falsifier: A hosting-abuse report, the provider's allocation record, or the content disappearing after a takedown would move the second claim.

site.name: Site C
evidence: The /24 is announced by StarHub, Singapore, so the space is operated even though the registry calls it reserved: a stale record.
No address serves a page: six refuse the connection and the rest time out, which is ordinary filtering on an announced range where no service runs.
The geography test passes: 170-181 ms is consistent with the announced operator's location.
site.falsifier: A page appearing on one of these addresses, or a refusal that moves between passes, would reopen the question.

site.name: Site D
site.confidence: Low; the device that resets is not identified
evidence: The responses come from individually used addresses inside 199.47.167.0/24, which is announced although the containing /21 has neither an announcement nor an RDAP object.
Two refusals and four resets, scattered as singles and one adjacent pair, look like hosts that exist and reject port 80.
Nothing identifies the filtering device, so the reading stays open.
site.falsifier: A traceroute or a measurement from an independent vantage point would place the reset source; a repeat pass would show whether the reset set moves.
